```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  eval = TRUE, collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
  message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
  fig.width = 11, fig.height = 5,
  out.width = "100%", fig.align = "center", cache = TRUE,
  cache.path = "inla-stan-model-comparisons_cache/html/"

library(surveyPrev)
library(SUMMER)
library(ggplot2)
library(rdhs)
INLA::inla.setOption(num.threads = "1:1")
```

This vignette compares the INLA and Stan implementations available through
`surveyPrev` and `SUMMER`, and then describes the internal organization of the
Stan backend.

# Comparing surveyPrev Model Classes with INLA and Stan

This section compares the main `surveyPrev` model classes using the 2024 Zambia
DHS indicator for four or more antenatal care visits. The data are downloaded
directly from the DHS website using **rdhs**. This step requires users to

1. register with DHS to gain data access, and
2. set up their DHS account login details with `rdhs::set_rdhs_config()`.

```{r surveyPrev-data}
dhs_raw <- getDHSdata(
  country = "Zambia", year = 2024, indicator = "RH_ANCN_W_N4P"
)
anc <- getDHSindicator(dhs_raw, indicator = "RH_ANCN_W_N4P")
gps <- getDHSgeo(country = "Zambia", year = 2024)

data(ZambiaAdm1)
data(ZambiaAdm2)
data(ZambiaPopWomen)
cluster_info <- clusterInfo(gps, ZambiaAdm1, ZambiaAdm2)
admin1_info <- adminInfo(
  ZambiaAdm1, admin = 1, by.adm = "NAME_1",
  agg.pop = ZambiaPopWomen$admin1_pop,
  proportion = ZambiaPopWomen$admin1_urban
)
admin2_info <- adminInfo(
  ZambiaAdm2, admin = 2, by.adm = "NAME_2", by.adm.upper = "NAME_1",
  agg.pop = ZambiaPopWomen$admin2_pop,
  proportion = ZambiaPopWomen$admin2_urban
)
```

Every Stan fit in this vignette uses three chains, 2,000 iterations per chain,
and 1,000 warmup iterations per chain. This leaves 1,000 retained draws per
chain and 3,000 retained draws in total. The common sampler arguments and
comparison plot are defined once below.

```{r comparison-helpers}
stan_args <- list(
  stan.chains = 3,
  stan.iter = 2000,
  stan.warmup = 1000,
  stan.seed = 1,
  stan.cores = 3
)

fit_both <- function(args, model_fun = NULL) {
  if (is.null(model_fun)) {
    return(list(
      INLA = do.call(SUMMER::smoothSurvey, c(args, list(nsim = 1000))),
      Stan = do.call(surveyPrev::smoothSurveyStan, c(args, stan_args))
    ))
  }

  list(
    INLA = do.call(model_fun, c(args, list(engine = "INLA"))),
    Stan = do.call(model_fun, c(args, list(engine = "rstan"), stan_args))
  )
}

model_table <- function(x, table = NULL) {
  if (!is.null(table)) {
    if (is.null(x[[table]])) stop("Model output has no table named '", table, "'.")
    return(x[[table]])
  }
  candidates <- c("res.admin1", "res.admin2", "agg.admin1", "smooth")
  for (name in candidates) if (!is.null(x[[name]])) return(x[[name]])
  stop("No model estimate table found.")
}

comparison_scatter <- function(pair, title, table = NULL) {
  x <- model_table(pair$INLA, table)
  y <- model_table(pair$Stan, table)
  keys <- intersect(
    c("admin1.name", "admin2.name.full", "region", "time", "strata", "type"),
    intersect(names(x), names(y))
  )

  x$.se <- if ("sd" %in% names(x)) x$sd else sqrt(x$var)
  y$.se <- if ("sd" %in% names(y)) y$sd else sqrt(y$var)
  if (length(keys)) {
    x[keys] <- lapply(x[keys], as.character)
    y[keys] <- lapply(y[keys], as.character)
    if (anyDuplicated(x[keys]) || anyDuplicated(y[keys])) {
      stop(
        "The available comparison keys do not uniquely identify model estimates: ",
        paste(keys, collapse = ", "), "."
      )
    }
    x <- x[, c(keys, "mean", ".se")]
    y <- y[, c(keys, "mean", ".se")]
    names(x)[names(x) %in% c("mean", ".se")] <- c("INLA_mean", "INLA_se")
    names(y)[names(y) %in% c("mean", ".se")] <- c("Stan_mean", "Stan_se")
    matched <- merge(x, y, by = keys, all = TRUE, sort = TRUE)
  } else {
    if (nrow(x) != nrow(y)) {
      stop("INLA and Stan outputs have different numbers of estimates.")
    }
    matched <- data.frame(
      INLA_mean = x$mean, INLA_se = x$.se,
      Stan_mean = y$mean, Stan_se = y$.se
    )
  }

  values <- c("INLA_mean", "INLA_se", "Stan_mean", "Stan_se")
  if (anyNA(matched[values])) {
    stop("INLA and Stan outputs do not have the same prediction keys.")
  }
  points <- rbind(
    data.frame(metric = "estimate", INLA = matched$INLA_mean,
               Stan = matched$Stan_mean),
    data.frame(metric = "standard error", INLA = matched$INLA_se,
               Stan = matched$Stan_se)
  )
  axis_bounds <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(points, points$metric),
    function(z) {
      values <- c(z$INLA, z$Stan)
      values <- values[is.finite(values)]
      limits <- if (length(values)) range(values) else c(0, 1)
      if (diff(limits) == 0) limits <- limits + c(-0.5, 0.5)
      data.frame(metric = z$metric[1], INLA = limits, Stan = limits)
    }
  ))
  ggplot(points, aes(INLA, Stan)) +
    geom_blank(data = axis_bounds) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "grey60",
                linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_point() +
    facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free") +
    labs(title = title) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(aspect.ratio = 1)
}
```

## Fay--Herriot Model with an IID Area Effect at Admin 1

```{r fh-iid}
fh_iid <- fit_both(list(
  data = anc, cluster.info = cluster_info, admin.info = admin1_info,
  admin = 1, model = "iid", aggregation = FALSE
), model_fun = fhModel)
comparison_scatter(fh_iid, "Fay-Herriot IID, admin 1")
```

Some computational checks are available using `diagModel()`.

```{r fh-iid-diagnostics}
diagModel(fh_iid$INLA)
diagModel(fh_iid$Stan)
```

## Fay--Herriot Model with a BYM2 Area Effect at Admin 1

```{r fh-bym2}
fh_bym2 <- fit_both(list(
  data = anc, cluster.info = cluster_info, admin.info = admin1_info,
  admin = 1, model = "bym2", aggregation = TRUE
), model_fun = fhModel)
comparison_scatter(fh_bym2, "Fay-Herriot BYM2, admin 1")
```

## Fay--Herriot Model with Nested BYM2 Effects at Admin 2

The sparse admin-2 direct estimates require the explicit variance-fix estimator.

```{r fh-nested}
fh_nested <- fit_both(list(
  data = anc, cluster.info = cluster_info, admin.info = admin2_info,
  admin = 2, model = "bym2", nested = TRUE, aggregation = FALSE,
  var.fix = TRUE
), model_fun = fhModel)
comparison_scatter(fh_nested, "Fay-Herriot nested BYM2 with variance fix")
```

```{r cluster-iid}
cluster_iid <- fit_both(list(
  data = anc, cluster.info = cluster_info, admin.info = admin1_info,

```

  data = anc, cluster.info = cluster_info, admin.info = admin1_info,

  data = anc, cluster.info = cluster_info, admin.info = admin2_info,

# Comparing Models from SUMMER::smoothSurvey with INLA and Stan

This section compares the INLA implementation in `SUMMER::smoothSurvey()` with
the Stan implementation in `surveyPrev::smoothSurveyStan()`.

The `smoothSurvey` examples use the same sampler settings, `fit_both()` helper,
and `comparison_scatter()` function defined above. All 3,000 retained Stan
draws are used in SUMMER's post-processing; if supplied, `nsim` is overwritten
by this retained draw count for the Stan fit.

We will go through major use cases for the `smoothSurvey` function using the examples with the demo datasets.

```{r demo-data}
data(DemoData2, package = "SUMMER")
data(DemoMap2, package = "SUMMER")
Xmat <- aggregate(age ~ region, DemoData2, mean)
base_binary <- list(
  data = DemoData2, Amat = DemoMap2$Amat, response.type = "binary",
  responseVar = "tobacco.use", strataVar = "strata",
  weightVar = "weights", regionVar = "region",
  clusterVar = "~clustid+id", CI = 0.95
)
```

## Area-level FH model with binary outcome, BYM2 prior

```{r area-binary-bym2}
area_binary <- fit_both(base_binary)
comparison_scatter(area_binary, "Area-level binary BYM2")
```

## Area-level FH model with binary outcome, SAR prior

```{r area-binary-sar}
area_sar <- fit_both(c(base_binary, list(space.model = "sar")))
comparison_scatter(area_sar, "Area-level binary SAR")
```

## Area-level FH model with binary outcome, unmatched link function

```{r area-unmatched}
area_unmatched <- fit_both(c(base_binary, list(unmatched.link = TRUE)))
comparison_scatter(area_unmatched, "Area-level unmatched link")
```

## Area-level FH model with covariate

```{r area-covariate}
area_covariate <- fit_both(c(base_binary, list(X = Xmat)))
comparison_scatter(area_covariate, "Area-level covariate")
```

## Area-level FH model with direct estimates of prevalence

```{r direct-binary}
direct_binary <- area_binary$INLA$direct[, c("region", "direct.est", "direct.var")]
direct_binary_fit <- fit_both(list(
  data = NULL, direct.est = direct_binary, Amat = DemoMap2$Amat,
  regionVar = "region", responseVar = "direct.est",
  direct.est.var = "direct.var", response.type = "binary"
))
comparison_scatter(direct_binary_fit, "Binary direct-estimate input")
```

## Area-level FH model with direct estimates of a Gaussian outcome

```{r direct-logit}
direct_logit <- area_binary$INLA$direct[
  , c("region", "direct.logit.est", "direct.logit.var")
]
direct_logit_fit <- fit_both(list(
  data = NULL, direct.est = direct_logit, Amat = DemoMap2$Amat,
  regionVar = "region", responseVar = "direct.logit.est",
  direct.est.var = "direct.logit.var", response.type = "gaussian"
))
comparison_scatter(direct_logit_fit, "Gaussian logit direct-estimate input")
```


## Unit-level model with binary outcome

```{r unit-binary}
unit_data <- DemoData2
unit_data$urbanicity <- ifelse(grepl("urban", unit_data$strata),
                               "urban", "rural")
unit_binary <- fit_both(list(
  data = unit_data, Amat = DemoMap2$Amat, response.type = "binary",
  X = Xmat, is.unit.level = TRUE, responseVar = "tobacco.use",
  strataVar.within = "urbanicity", regionVar = "region",
  clusterVar = "clustid", CI = 0.95
))
comparison_scatter(unit_binary, "Unit-level beta-binomial")
```

## Unit-level model with aggregated cluster counts

```{r unit-binary-aggregated}
counts <- aggregate(tobacco.use ~ region + urbanicity + clustid,
                    unit_data, sum)
totals <- aggregate(tobacco.use ~ region + urbanicity + clustid,
                    unit_data, length)
names(totals)[4] <- "total"
counts <- merge(counts, totals)
unit_counts <- fit_both(list(
  data = counts, Amat = DemoMap2$Amat, response.type = "binary",
  X = Xmat, is.unit.level = TRUE, is.agg = TRUE,
  responseVar = "tobacco.use", strataVar.within = "urbanicity",
  totalVar = "total", regionVar = "region", clusterVar = "clustid"
))
comparison_scatter(unit_counts, "Aggregated beta-binomial")
```

## Area-level model with Gaussian outcome

```{r area-gaussian}
area_gaussian <- fit_both(list(
  data = DemoData2, Amat = DemoMap2$Amat, response.type = "gaussian",
  responseVar = "age", strataVar = "strata", weightVar = "weights",
  regionVar = "region", clusterVar = "~clustid+id"
))
comparison_scatter(area_gaussian, "Area-level Gaussian")
```

## Unit-level nested-error model

The sample response and satellite covariates are from 12 Iowa counties. The
county-level covariate means are supplied in `X` for prediction.

```{r corn-soybean, cache.lazy=FALSE}
data(cornsoybean, package = "sae")
data(cornsoybeanmeans, package = "sae")
cornsoybean <- cornsoybean[-33, , drop = FALSE] # remove outlier
cornsoybean_X <- data.frame(cornsoybeanmeans[
  , c("CountyIndex", "MeanCornPixPerSeg", "MeanSoyBeansPixPerSeg")
])
names(cornsoybean_X) <- c("County", "CornPix", "SoyBeansPix")

cornsoybean_pair <- fit_both(list(
  data = cornsoybean, X.unit = c("CornPix", "SoyBeansPix"),
  X = cornsoybean_X, Amat = NULL,
  response.type = "gaussian", is.unit.level = TRUE,
  responseVar = "CornHec", regionVar = "County", clusterVar = NULL,
  pc.u = 1000, pc.alpha = 0.01, CI = 0.95
))
comparison_scatter(cornsoybean_pair,
                   "Corn and soybean nested-error model")
```

## Neonatal mortality with RW2 and Type I--IV interactions

```{r nmr-data}
data(DemoData, package = "SUMMER")
data(DemoMap, package = "SUMMER")
nmr_births <- lapply(DemoData, function(x) {
  x[as.character(x$age) == "0", , drop = FALSE]
})
names(nmr_births) <- names(DemoData)
periods <- levels(DemoData[[1]]$time)
nmr_multi <- SUMMER::getDirectList(
  births = nmr_births, years = periods, regionVar = "region",
  timeVar = "time", clusterVar = "~clustid+id", ageVar = "age",
  weightsVar = "weights"
)
nmr_direct <- SUMMER::aggregateSurvey(nmr_multi)
nmr_direct <- subset(nmr_direct, region != "All")
nmr_direct$time_index <- match(nmr_direct$years, periods)
nmr_direct$variance <- nmr_direct$var.est *
  (nmr_direct$mean * (1 - nmr_direct$mean))^2
```

```{r nmr-fits, cache.lazy=FALSE}
nmr_type_labels <- paste("Type", c("I", "II", "III", "IV"))
nmr_pairs <- setNames(vector("list", 4), nmr_type_labels)
for (interaction in 1:4) {
  label <- nmr_type_labels[interaction]
  nmr_pairs[[label]] <- fit_both(list(
    data = NULL, direct.est = nmr_direct, Amat = DemoMap$Amat,
    regionVar = "region", timeVar = "time_index",
    responseVar = "mean", direct.est.var = "variance",
    response.type = "binary", time.model = "rw2",
    type.st = interaction
  ))
}
```
We compare the estimates and standard errors for all four fits below. 

```{r nmr-probability-comparison}
for (label in nmr_type_labels) {
  print(comparison_scatter(
    nmr_pairs[[label]],
    paste("Neonatal mortality probability: RW2 +", label)
  ))
}
```

For the four NMR models, we also compare posterior means and 95% credible intervals
for the intercept, variance and mixing parameters, main spatial and temporal
effects, and every region-by-period interaction. INLA precision
parameters are transformed to standard deviations so that they have the same
interpretation as the corresponding Stan parameters. The BYM2 spatial effect
shown below is the combined structured and unstructured effect used in the
linear predictor. Thus, every latent random effect entering the predictor is
compared on the model's logit scale. Each point is a posterior mean, each line
is a central 95% credible interval, and color identifies INLA or rstan. Within
each panel, the x-axis groups the four interaction types so that each type has
one INLA--rstan pair.

```{r nmr-parameter-comparison, fig.width=16, fig.height=7.5, cache=FALSE}
nmr_fits <- lapply(nmr_pairs, function(pair) {
  list(
    inla = pair$INLA$fit,
    stan = pair$Stan$fit$stanfit,
    draws = rstan::extract(pair$Stan$fit$stanfit, permuted = TRUE)
  )
})
nmr_regions <- colnames(DemoMap$Amat)
nmr_times <- sort(unique(nmr_direct$time_index))
nmr_time_labels <- periods[nmr_times]

inla_interval <- function(marginal, transform = identity) {
  clean_marginal <- function(x) {
    x <- as.matrix(x)
    x <- x[is.finite(x[, 1]) & is.finite(x[, 2]), , drop = FALSE]
    x <- x[order(x[, 1]), , drop = FALSE]
    if (anyDuplicated(x[, 1])) {
      x <- stats::aggregate(x[, 2], list(x[, 1]), mean)
    }
    if (nrow(x) < 2L) stop("The INLA marginal has too few finite points.")
    as.matrix(x)
  }
  marginal <- clean_marginal(marginal)
  marginal <- INLA::inla.tmarginal(transform, marginal)
  marginal <- clean_marginal(marginal)
  c(
    mean = unname(INLA::inla.emarginal(identity, marginal)),
    lower = unname(INLA::inla.qmarginal(0.025, marginal)),
    upper = unname(INLA::inla.qmarginal(0.975, marginal))
  )
}

stan_intervals <- function(draws, parameter, component, interaction_type) {
  if (length(dim(draws)) < 2L) draws <- matrix(draws, ncol = 1)
  if (ncol(draws) != length(parameter)) {
    stop("The number of rstan parameters does not match its labels.")
  }
  intervals <- t(apply(draws, 2, function(x) {
    c(mean = mean(x), quantile(x, c(0.025, 0.975), names = FALSE))
  }))
  data.frame(
    component = component, parameter = parameter,
    mean = intervals[, 1], lower = intervals[, 2], upper = intervals[, 3],
    method = "rstan", interaction_type = interaction_type, row.names = NULL
  )
}

inla_random_intervals <- function(fit, name, n, parameter, component,
                                  interaction_type, index = seq_len(n)) {
  x <- fit$summary.random[[name]]
  if (is.null(x) || nrow(x) < n || length(parameter) != n ||
      length(index) != n || any(index < 1L | index > nrow(x))) {
    stop("The INLA random-effect dimensions do not match their labels.")
  }
  x <- x[index, ]
  data.frame(
    component = component, parameter = parameter,
    mean = x$mean, lower = x$`0.025quant`, upper = x$`0.975quant`,
    method = "INLA", interaction_type = interaction_type, row.names = NULL
  )
}

inla_hyper_intervals <- function(fit, name, parameter, interaction_type,
                                 transform = identity,
                                 component = "Scale parameters") {
  marginal <- fit$internal.marginals.hyperpar[[name]]
  if (is.null(marginal)) {
    stop("The INLA hyperparameter marginal was not found: ", name)
  }
  z <- inla_interval(marginal, transform)
  data.frame(
    component = component, parameter = parameter,
    mean = z["mean"], lower = z["lower"], upper = z["upper"],
    method = "INLA", interaction_type = interaction_type, row.names = NULL
  )
}

comparison_axis <- function(data, parameter_levels) {
  data$interaction_type <- factor(data$interaction_type, nmr_type_labels)
  axis_levels <- as.vector(t(outer(
    parameter_levels, nmr_type_labels, paste, sep = "\n"
  )))
  data$parameter_type <- factor(
    paste(data$parameter, data$interaction_type, sep = "\n"), axis_levels
  )
  data
}

interval_plot <- function(data, x) {
  dodge <- position_dodge(width = 0.55)
  ggplot(data, aes(x = {{ x }}, y = mean, colour = method, group = method)) +
    geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
                   position = dodge, linewidth = 0.45) +
    geom_point(position = dodge, size = 1.5) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(INLA = "#0072B2", rstan = "#D55E00")) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Posterior value", colour = NULL) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "top", panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
    )
}

nmr_global <- do.call(rbind, lapply(nmr_type_labels, function(type) {
  inla_fit <- nmr_fits[[type]]$inla
  draws <- nmr_fits[[type]]$draws
  inla_fixed <- inla_fit$summary.fixed
  interaction_name <- if (type %in% c("Type II", "Type IV")) {
    "time.area"
  } else {
    "region.int"
  }
  rbind(
    data.frame(
      component = "Fixed effect", parameter = rownames(inla_fixed),
      mean = inla_fixed$mean, lower = inla_fixed$`0.025quant`,
      upper = inla_fixed$`0.975quant`, method = "INLA",
      interaction_type = type, row.names = NULL
    ),
    stan_intervals(
      draws$beta, rownames(inla_fixed), "Fixed effect", type
    ),
    inla_hyper_intervals(
      inla_fit, "Log precision for region.struct", "Spatial SD", type,
      function(x) exp(-x / 2)
    ),
    inla_hyper_intervals(
      inla_fit, "Logit phi for region.struct", "BYM2 phi", type, plogis,
      component = "Mixing parameter"
    ),
    inla_hyper_intervals(
      inla_fit, "Log precision for time.unstruct", "Temporal IID SD", type,
      function(x) exp(-x / 2)
    ),
    inla_hyper_intervals(
      inla_fit, "Log precision for time.struct", "Temporal RW2 SD", type,
      function(x) exp(-x / 2)
    ),
    inla_hyper_intervals(
      inla_fit, paste("Log precision for", interaction_name),
      "Interaction SD", type,
      function(x) exp(-x / 2)
    ),
    stan_intervals(
      draws$sigma_space, "Spatial SD", "Scale parameters", type
    ),
    stan_intervals(draws$phi, "BYM2 phi", "Mixing parameter", type),
    stan_intervals(
      draws$sigma_time_unstruct, "Temporal IID SD", "Scale parameters", type
    ),
    stan_intervals(
      draws$sigma_time_struct, "Temporal RW2 SD", "Scale parameters", type
    ),
    stan_intervals(
      draws$sigma_st, "Interaction SD", "Scale parameters", type
    )
  )
}))
nmr_global$method <- factor(nmr_global$method, c("INLA", "rstan"))
nmr_global <- comparison_axis(
  nmr_global,
  c("(Intercept)", "Spatial SD", "BYM2 phi", "Temporal IID SD",
    "Temporal RW2 SD", "Interaction SD")
)

interval_plot(nmr_global, parameter_type) +
  facet_wrap(~component, scales = "free")
```

```{r nmr-main-random-effects, fig.width=18, fig.height=7.5}
nmr_main_random <- do.call(rbind, lapply(nmr_type_labels, function(type) {
  inla_fit <- nmr_fits[[type]]$inla
  draws <- nmr_fits[[type]]$draws
  rbind(
    inla_random_intervals(
      inla_fit, "region.struct", length(nmr_regions), nmr_regions,
      "Spatial", type
    ),
    stan_intervals(draws$re_space, nmr_regions, "Spatial", type),
    inla_random_intervals(
      inla_fit, "time.unstruct", length(nmr_times), nmr_time_labels,
      "Temporal IID", type
    ),
    stan_intervals(
      draws$re_time_unstruct, nmr_time_labels, "Temporal IID", type
    ),
    inla_random_intervals(
      inla_fit, "time.struct", length(nmr_times), nmr_time_labels,
      "Temporal RW2", type
    ),
    stan_intervals(
      draws$re_time_struct, nmr_time_labels, "Temporal RW2", type
    )
  )
}))
nmr_main_random$method <- factor(nmr_main_random$method, c("INLA", "rstan"))
nmr_main_random <- comparison_axis(
  nmr_main_random, c(nmr_regions, nmr_time_labels)
)

interval_plot(nmr_main_random, parameter_type) +
  facet_wrap(~component, nrow = 1, scales = "free_x")
```

```{r nmr-interaction-effects, fig.width=16, fig.height=7.5}
nmr_interaction_index <- expand.grid(
  region = nmr_regions, time = nmr_time_labels,
  KEEP.OUT.ATTRS = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
nmr_interaction <- do.call(rbind, lapply(nmr_type_labels, function(type) {
  inla_name <- if (type %in% c("Type II", "Type IV")) {
    "time.area"
  } else {
    "region.int"
  }
  # INLA's Type II/IV generic0 fields are region-major; the other fields and
  # Stan are time-major, matching nmr_interaction_index.
  inla_index <- if (type %in% c("Type II", "Type IV")) {
    (match(nmr_interaction_index$region, nmr_regions) - 1L) *
      length(nmr_time_labels) +
      match(nmr_interaction_index$time, nmr_time_labels)
  } else {
    seq_len(nrow(nmr_interaction_index))
  }
  block <- rbind(
    inla_random_intervals(
      nmr_fits[[type]]$inla, inla_name, nrow(nmr_interaction_index),
      nmr_interaction_index$region, "Space-time interaction", type,
      index = inla_index
    ),
    stan_intervals(
      nmr_fits[[type]]$draws$re_st, nmr_interaction_index$region,
      "Space-time interaction", type
    )
  )
  block$time <- rep(nmr_interaction_index$time, times = 2)
  block
}))
nmr_interaction$method <- factor(nmr_interaction$method, c("INLA", "rstan"))
nmr_interaction$time <- factor(nmr_interaction$time, nmr_time_labels)
nmr_interaction <- comparison_axis(nmr_interaction, nmr_regions)

interval_plot(nmr_interaction, parameter_type) +
  facet_wrap(~time, nrow = 2)
```

# Understanding the Internal Design of the Stan Backend

The call path is

```text
smoothSurveyStan()
  -> SUMMER::smoothSurvey(.backend = ...)
       -> .stan_smoothSurvey_fit()
            -> fh_gaussian.stan or betabinom.stan
            -> posterior draws in the form expected by SUMMER
```

`SUMMER::smoothSurvey()` continues to perform the common survey-data
preparation and assemble the returned estimates. The functions in
`surveyPrev` translate that prepared model input to Stan and translate the
draws back to the small posterior interface used by SUMMER.

## Interface, Data Preparation, and Supporting Infrastructure

| Function | File | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `smoothSurveyStan()` | `R/smoothSurvey_stan.R` | Public entry point. Checks Stan-supported arguments, constructs the backend, and calls `SUMMER::smoothSurvey()`. Add or expose a new user-facing Stan option here. |
| `.stan_smoothSurvey_backend()` | `R/smoothSurvey_stan.R` | Creates the `fit`, linear-predictor, and posterior-sampling callbacks required by the SUMMER backend interface. Change this when the internal data structures change. |
| `.stan_smoothSurvey_fit()` | `R/smoothSurvey_stan.R` | Builds design matrices and Stan data, chooses the Gaussian or beta-binomial program, runs rstan, and renames posterior draws to match SUMMER's latent-field convention. Change this when the Stan input/output changes. |
| `.smoothSurvey_dispatch()` | `R/smoothSurvey_stan.R` | Internal INLA/rstan switch used by higher-level surveyPrev workflows. It is not the public model implementation. |
| `.get_stanmodel()` | `R/common_stan.R` | Locates, compiles, and caches a Stan program once per R session. |
| `get_fh_stanmodel()` and `get_betabinom_stanmodel()` | `R/common_stan.R` | Small model-specific loaders that identify the corresponding file under `inst/stan`. |
| `.validate_adjacency_stan()` | `R/common_stan.R` | Validates an adjacency matrix and converts row-standardized weights to an undirected binary edge matrix. |
| `.graph_components_stan()` | `R/common_stan.R` | Finds connected components and their sizes without requiring an additional graph package. |
| `.empty_spatial_data_stan()` | `R/common_stan.R` | Supplies shape-compatible placeholder graph data when a Besag graph is not used. |
| `.stan_sampling_args()` | `R/common_stan.R` | Centralizes chain, iteration, seed, core, and HMC-control arguments passed to `rstan::sampling()`. |
| `.type4_inla_components()` | `SUMMER/R/type4-inla.R` | Builds the scaled Kronecker precision and connected-component constraints for the INLA `smoothSurvey()` Type IV implementation, mirroring `smoothDirect()`. Its constraint subspace is also mirrored in Stan. |
| `diagModel()` and `.find_model_fit()` | `R/diagModel.R` | Find an INLA or rstan fit inside the supported result wrappers and provide the common diagnostics interface. |
| `.diag_stan()` | `R/diagModel_stan.R` | Computes rstan-specific divergence, treedepth, R-hat, effective-sample-size, and E-BFMI checks. |

The `.backend` argument in `SUMMER::smoothSurvey()` is the boundary between
the two packages. Changes to survey design processing, direct-estimate
construction, or final aggregation normally belong in SUMMER. Changes to
Stan data construction, sampling, or draw extraction belong in
`.stan_smoothSurvey_fit()`.

## Model-Specific Preparation and Prior Specification

| Function | File | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `.smoothsurvey_spatial_data_stan()` | `R/smoothSurvey_stan.R` | Converts `space.model` and `type.st` into Stan model codes, prepares BYM2/Besag graph data, and constructs the row-standardized matrix used by SAR. |
| `.rw_scaling_factor_stan()` | `R/common_stan.R` | Computes the generalized-variance scaling used for RW1 and RW2 effects so their scale parameters have a stable interpretation. |
| `.prepare_bym2_graph_stan()` | `R/common_stan.R` | Scales every connected ICAR component, handles singleton regions, creates edge and constraint indices, and prepares either the INLA-tabulated or analytic spectral BYM2 `phi` prior. This is the main R function to inspect when revising BYM2 behavior. |
| `stan_betabinomial()` | `R/clusterModel_stan.R` | Builds and fits the non-temporal beta-binomial model used by `clusterModel()`, then creates its INLA-compatible prediction and latent-draw objects. It shares `betabinom.stan` and the graph helpers with `smoothSurveyStan()`, but is not called by `smoothSurveyStan()`. |

The general PC scale-prior rate is computed in R as
`lambda = -log(pc.alpha) / pc.u`. Fixed-effect precisions, beta-binomial
overdispersion hyperparameters, graph scaling constants, and BYM2 `phi` prior
inputs are also created in R. Their actual contribution to the posterior is
defined in the Stan `model` blocks.

## Stan Model Specification

| Program or block | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `inst/stan/fh_gaussian.stan` | Gaussian Fay--Herriot likelihoods with known sampling variance, unmatched-link models, and unit-level Gaussian models with estimated residual precision. |
| `inst/stan/betabinom.stan` | Beta-binomial likelihood and overdispersion model used for unit-level binary `smoothSurveyStan()` fits and `clusterModel()` fits. |
| `interpolate_lpdf()` in the `functions` block | Linearly interpolates the tabulated INLA BYM2 log-density supplied by R. |
| `pc_bym2_phi_lpdf()` in the `functions` block | Evaluates the alternative analytic spectral BYM2 `phi` density. |
| `data` | Declares the interface produced by `.stan_smoothSurvey_fit()` or `stan_betabinomial()`. Any declaration change must be matched in the corresponding R data list. |
| `parameters` | Declares fixed effects, scale and mixing parameters, unscaled spatial, temporal, and interaction effects, and the unpenalized RW2 slope directions retained by `smoothDirect()`. |
| `transformed parameters` | Constructs the BYM2, SAR, temporal, and Type I--IV effects that enter the linear predictor, including their scaling and separate RW2 linear trends. |
| `model` | Defines fixed-effect and PC priors, BYM2/Besag penalties, constraints, RW1/RW2 penalties, Type I--IV interaction structures, and the observation likelihood. |
| `generated quantities` | Returns linear predictors and, for the beta-binomial model, predicted probabilities consumed by the R adapters. |

The two Stan programs intentionally use the same spatial, temporal,
interaction, constraint, and BYM2-prior formulation. A revision to any of
those shared model components should therefore be made in both programs and
tested for both likelihoods.

## Where to Modify the Stan Backend

| Intended revision | Start here | Also check |
|---|---|---|
| Change a likelihood or add an observation-level parameter | The relevant file in `inst/stan` | The Stan data and extraction code in `.stan_smoothSurvey_fit()`; for cluster models, `stan_betabinomial()` |
| Change a prior already implemented in Stan | The `model` block in both Stan programs | The R construction of its hyperparameters in `.stan_smoothSurvey_fit()` or `.prepare_bym2_graph_stan()` |
| Change the BYM2 `phi` prior | `.prepare_bym2_graph_stan()` and the Stan `functions`/`model` blocks | Both Stan programs and graph-prior tests |
| Change disconnected-graph or ICAR scaling behavior | `.validate_adjacency_stan()`, `.graph_components_stan()`, and `.prepare_bym2_graph_stan()` | BYM2 and Type III/IV code in both Stan programs |
| Change RW1, RW2, or Type I--IV interactions | `transformed parameters` and `model` in both Stan programs | `.rw_scaling_factor_stan()`, model codes in `.stan_smoothSurvey_fit()`, and linear-predictor indexing |
| Change identifiability constraints | The `constr` sections of both Stan `model` blocks | Graph-component metadata and `constr` propagation from `smoothSurveyStan()` |
| Add a public model or sampler argument | `smoothSurveyStan()` | `.stan_smoothSurvey_backend()`, `.stan_smoothSurvey_fit()`, and documentation |
| Change returned latent effects or predictions | Generated quantities in Stan and extraction in `.stan_smoothSurvey_fit()` | The backend callbacks and SUMMER's expected latent names |
| Change diagnostic thresholds or checks | `diagModel()` or `.diag_stan()` | Tests in `tests/testthat/test-diagModel.R` |

After changing either Stan program, first run `rstan::stanc()` on the modified
file to check its syntax. Then test the affected likelihood, spatial model,
temporal model, and interaction type; changes to shared random-effect code
should be tested against both Stan programs.
